milestone: Dev Graph milestone 1, ticket 'Revision contracts, candidate versioning and assessment applicability'
authority: CLAUDE.md §9.4 (durable decisions), §12.2 (status vocabulary; nothing here approves), §13.3 (no invented facts), §17.5.3 (deterministic components), §16.5 (bindable vocabulary). Not a constitutional amendment.
decision: A revision is checked by a pure contract checker over the recorded change set, a new candidate version is a second immutable document snapshot that supersedes the first through an edge derived from its provenance, and an assessment's applicability is a pure comparison of its binding against the current candidate, profile and policy versions. Assessments are never mutated; unresolved items are never approved.

contract_checker.entry_point: runner.dev_graph.revisions.check_revision(contract, change_set). Pure: no I/O, no clock. The contract is normalised first (normalise_contract) and refuses an unknown change class, a non-identifier node id, or an unresolved item with any status but unresolved.
contract_checker.change_classes: A change set is classified by closed lookup, never by inference. An added or removed edge takes the class of its predicate (assigned_to responsibility, contributes_to contribution, consumes dependency, produces output, validated_by validation, constrained_by constraint, supported_by evidence, expressed_in/addresses/supersedes wording). An added or removed node takes the class of its type. A directly changed node takes the class of each changed field where the (type, field) pair is in the table (responsible_partner responsibility, contributing_partners contribution, dependencies dependency, start_month/end_month/due_month timing, lead_partner responsibility, objectives contribution, constraints constraint, produced_by output, deliverables validation) and its type's class otherwise. A contained change carries no class. The three tables cover every predicate and every node type; an import-time assertion pins that.
contract_checker.changed_fields: change_set gained a changed_fields list on direct node changes and nodes.added/removed items now carry id and type, so the checker needs no snapshot. The impact planner reads the new shape; the change record spec (5.7) is updated.
contract_checker.verdicts: rejected when the change touches a protected node: the node is named with the reasons it is touched (changed:<id> or the changed edge labels). Otherwise flagged_for_review when a change class is not permitted or an unresolved item bears on the change. Otherwise accepted. Rejection outranks review; every hit and every unpermitted class is kept in the result.
contract_checker.unresolved_items: An item names node_ids; it bears on the change when any of them is touched. An item with no node_ids bears on every change under the contract. The item is carried into the result with status unresolved and bears_on_change; the checker has no path that sets any other status. An unresolved participant capacity therefore stays flagged in every result and is never approved (§12.2).

candidate_versioning.entry_point: runner.dev_graph.revisions.create_candidate_version(repo_root, candidate_rel, supersedes=, change_id=, evidence=). Refuses before writing when the predecessor or an evidence node is absent from the current build, the change record does not exist, or the content equals the snapshot it would supersede.
candidate_versioning.provenance: The new document record carries provenance {supersedes: {id, version}, change_id, evidence: [{id, version}]}, resolved against the current snapshot at creation and stored as given. The builder emits artifact_version supersedes artifact_version from it; validate_graph reports a dangling predecessor.
candidate_versioning.old_record: The superseded record is left byte for byte as it was. Its lifecycle state is not rewritten to superseded; the edge carries the fact, and current_commitments excludes any snapshot that is the target of a supersedes edge. Rewriting the state would make the old record a second writer of a fact the new record already owns.
candidate_versioning.immutability: Re-running with the same inputs lands on the same path with the same bytes. The same content under other provenance or another state is refused with immutable_record (the document import's state-change refusal moves to that kind too, since it is the same condition).

applicability.entry_point: runner.dev_graph.revisions.check_applicability(assessment, candidate, profile_version=, policy_version=). bind_assessment builds the assessment node whose content carries the binding {candidate: {id, version}, profile_version, policy_version}; the binding is inside the content so the node version pins it.
applicability.reasons: candidate_version_changed when the bound candidate id or version differs from the current one; profile_version_changed and policy_version_changed likewise. All applicable reasons are listed, in that order; applicable is true only with none.
applicability.never_mutated: The assessment node is read and never written; the result is a separate value naming the assessment by id and version. No field on the assessment records applicability.

writer: dev_graph_revision_record_writer is a registered deterministic component. It reads dev_graph/revision_request.json ({revision_id, change_id, contract, candidate, supersedes, evidence}), loads the change record, runs the check, creates the candidate version only on accepted, and writes dev_graph/revisions/<revision_id>.json with the contract, the check and the created version with its provenance. A revision id is write-once: the same inputs replay byte-equal; other content under an existing id is refused. A rejected or flagged check is recorded honestly with candidate_version null and no document written. No wall-clock field; the component's run id does not enter the artifact. Registered as artifact 5.11 in artifact_schema_specification.yaml and in docs/index/schema_registry.json (§9.6). It is registered in the component registry but bound to no manifest node, like the other dev-graph writers: no workflow node invokes it, an operator does. §16.5 binding applies when a node body declares it; that declaration is not part of milestone 1.
not_done_here: indexing change records or revision contracts as change_request and revision_contract nodes (the types stay in the closed set for the harness lane).
the harness pre-evaluation profile and the candidate-bound blind assessment (their own tickets).
the end-to-end T03 scenario test (milestone closure ticket).
verification: tests/runner/test_dev_graph_revisions.py: a responsibility change under a permitting contract is accepted with class responsibility only; a change that also alters the protected objective is rejected naming OBJ-1; a removed edge to a protected deliverable is a hit; an unpermitted timing change is flagged; an unresolved capacity the change bears on stays flagged and no result text contains approved; an item the change does not touch is carried unresolved; rejection outranks review; the checker is pure; malformed contracts and change sets are refused. Versioning: a second snapshot supersedes the first with provenance and the first's bytes are unchanged; the superseded snapshot yields no current commitment; re-import is a no-op and other provenance is refused; unknown predecessor, change or evidence refuses before writing; self-supersession refuses. Applicability: applicable against version one, candidate_version_changed against version two, profile and policy each their own reason, all three together, the assessment unchanged after the check. Writer: registered and Claude-free; byte-equal replay through the registry; a rejected check records the verdict and creates no version; write-once; a missing change record or malformed request refuses and writes nothing; the lint covers revisions.py.
